_comment: The ancient orders and classes of Plato's dialogues (milestone 9). Every item quotes the source that states it; tools/structure.py finds each quotation in texts/ancient/ when the library is built and refuses an item whose quotation is not found. 'work' is the Perseus id; 'name', 'subtitle' and 'character' are as the translation prints them. Read and chosen by hand from the texts; nothing is inferred.

orders.label: Albinus' order
orders.about: For the reader well born, of the age for philosophy and drawn away from politics. Albinus also reports that some begin with the Epistles or the Theages, and rejects the tetralogies as an order for teaching.

orders.label: The Iamblichean curriculum
orders.by: Iamblichus (c. 245-325), as reported by the Anonymous Prolegomena (6th century)
orders.about: Twelve dialogues, physical and theological, gathered into two, the Timaeus and the Parmenides. The order of the rest follows the grades of virtue (political, purificatory, theoretical). In Hermann's text the dialogue that follows the Theaetetus is not named, only described as 'the one teaching about natural things'; it is left unnamed here.
